correctness.rationale: For every alternating even factor cycle, choose a root of an internal red matching chord. In the ordered cycle-edge block, put its red edge between first B and final H, while every other red chord is inserted after the later cycle edge of the lower-index endpoint and before the earlier edge of the higher-index endpoint. Cross-cycle red matching edges go after their earlier cycle block. Thus root red is middle, all other red entries are first or last; B/H-relative order alternates along cycle edges away from the root, and every red edge has first-last or first-middle endpoint positions. This exhausts all edge types. The included stdlib verifier checks all 3655 one-cycle admissible chord matchings over lengths 4 through 12, 972 sampled valid multi-cycle profiles, and 25 Möbius ladder sizes. These finite checks are not used as the universal proof.

The earlier indexed edge-ordering result concerns bipartite graphs. The present assertion also covers nonbipartite cubic graphs with uniform palettes, including all antipodal-matching cycle graphs of order divisible by four. Thus it is not a corollary of these theorems . Targeted search found no covering full statement, but unindexed parallel work remains possible.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper explicitly leaves fixed proper three-edge-colourings of cubic graphs open. The theorem supplies a robust, linear-time construction for a natural and extensible graph-factor condition (a red matching chord on each component of the alternating two-colour 2-factor). It covers all fixed colourings with a bichromatic Hamiltonian cycle and infinitely many 2-connected, indeed 3-connected, nonbipartite cubic graphs, with no size restriction. This is a substantive structural positive case, not a normalization test or arbitrary finite constant.
